verdict.rationale: ROS 2 documents shipping message packages and a sensor-data QoS profile, and its own README says it covers everything 'from drivers to state-of-the-art algorithms'. Community users confirm a large ecosystem of existing drivers and shared message definitions that let packages interoperate without glue code. However, nothing in the evidence names drivers or message types for cameras, lidars, IMUs or GPS specifically. Missing for 10: documented ready-made drivers for cameras, lidars, IMUs and GPS; named standard sensor message types (e.g. image, point cloud, IMU, navsat); a hardware bring-up guide.

support.subject: As a robotics engineer, I can integrate cameras, lidars, IMUs, and GPS with ready-made drivers and standard message types

citations.quote: Communication libraries, message packages, command line tools.
ROS 2 provides a set of predefined QoS profiles for common use cases (e.g. sensor data).
The topic interface is meant for continuous data streams, for example, streaming sensor data or the status of your robot.
